findings.claim: The public record supports a sequence of institutional acts and observed distress; it does not support a character judgment that Chloe Moffat was weak or unable to tolerate ordinary workplace pressure.
limits: No diagnosis or private psychological inference is made.

findings.claim: The process produced formal-threat effects while retaining an informal fact-finding label, allowing the organization to withhold safeguards partly because providing them would make the meeting feel formal.
limits: Formality arbitrage is an analytical term, not a quoted legal category or final inquest finding.

findings.claim: A process label is an inadequate safeguard trigger when practical indicators already include a serious allegation, senior attendance, access restriction, confidentiality limits, and a contemplated formal investigation.
limits: The proposed severity trigger is not adopted policy or current law.

findings.claim: Refusing to bound a realistically unlikely dismissal outcome preserved maximum uncertainty at the point of visible distress.
limits: The packet does not claim that reassurance must be absolute or that an investigation outcome can always be promised.

findings.claim: Confidentiality and evidence-protection measures can become isolation mechanisms unless they expressly preserve access to a companion, union, healthcare, employee assistance, or independent welfare contact.
limits: The packet does not reject proportionate confidentiality or evidence preservation.

findings.claim: Assigning pastoral care to a manager embedded in the adverse process creates a care-control collision and weakens the independence of the safety function.
limits: Role conflict does not establish malicious intent or individual culpability.

findings.claim: Current accountability channels can route a severe individual event toward fact-finding, organizational learning, or population-level enforcement without necessarily producing an individual professional accountability ruling.
limits: This is a structural inference, not a prediction that no person will ever face accountability in this case.

findings.claim: The absence of a public individual sanction cannot be converted into proof that no institutional failure occurred, just as procedural reform cannot substitute for causal custody of the original decisions.
limits: The packet records no final inquest conclusion and no disciplinary record concerning any employee.

findings.claim: Avoidable employee harm is a supported systems concept: disciplinary investigations can produce distress and trauma, and an intervention that treated investigations as a last resort substantially reduced their use in one organization.
limits: The intervention evidence is not a case-specific counterfactual for Chloe Moffat.

findings.claim: The case exemplifies the welfare-control split in modern HR: the organization invokes pastoral care while the controlling process optimizes accusation handling, confidentiality, access restriction, and institutional defensibility.
limits: This finding connects the case to the estate genealogy; it does not claim that every HR function or employee behaves identically.

process_events.details: A complaint alleged that confidential information about colleagues had been shared.
limits: The complaint's truth, provenance, evidential weight, and motive are not adjudicated here.

process_events.details: The employee was not told in advance what the meeting would concern and therefore could not prepare or arrange support.
limits: The packet records the procedural contrast with Acas guidance; it does not decide legal breach.

process_events.details: The meeting was treated as early fact-finding while the employee faced serious allegations, senior attendance, access restriction, confidentiality instructions, and preparation for a formal investigation.
limits: The phrase formality arbitrage is an analytical classification introduced by this packet.

process_events.details: A request to bring a friend for support was refused; testimony said an alternative attendee would have made the meeting feel more formal.
limits: There is no automatic statutory accompaniment right at every investigatory meeting; Acas identifies allowance as good practice.

process_events.details: When the employee asked whether dismissal was possible, a senior manager declined to predict the outcome even though evidence reported to the inquest indicated dismissal was unlikely.
limits: This does not establish what every lawful or reasonable manager would have said.

process_events.details: The employee temporarily lost access to the director's email and diary and was instructed not to discuss the matter with colleagues.
limits: Interim restrictions can serve legitimate evidence-protection aims; proportionality and support carve-outs remain open.

process_events.details: Witness evidence described shock, crying, and acute fear about job loss and reputational consequences.
limits: The packet does not diagnose a medical condition or infer private mental-health history.

process_events.details: The line manager was expected to provide pastoral care while also occupying a direct oversight role in the process.
limits: The packet identifies role conflict; it does not assign personal blame.

process_events.details: After the employee denied the allegations, a letter opening a formal investigation was being drafted but had not yet been sent.
limits: The eventual investigation outcome cannot be recovered because the process did not reach it.

process_events.details: Chloe Olivia Moffat died on 20 May 2025, the day after the meeting described in public reporting.
limits: Temporal sequence alone is not a final coroner finding of causation.

process_events.details: The Treasury reported procedural changes, advice work, and additional manager training.
limits: No public record recovered for this wave establishes individual sanction, professional discipline, or a completed accountability ruling.

prohibited_inferences: Chloe Moffat was weak, irrational, or unable to tolerate ordinary workplace pressure.
Any named manager, HR professional, complainant, or Treasury employee caused the death or is individually culpable.
The anonymous allegation was true or false.
The meeting breached a statutory accompaniment right.
The coroner has issued a final conclusion or assigned legal liability.
All informal investigations are unsafe or all confidentiality restrictions are illegitimate.
Procedural reform proves the original process was lawful, safe, or complete.
title: Chloe Moffat: formal-threat effects under an informal fact-finding label
